mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi ASX 1.6 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt 4A92 engine supply-only typically costs £1,200-£2,200, with used units from £400-£900 and reconditioned from £900-£1,800 [ESTIMATED - using nearest-family proxy 2ZR-FE 1.8 from Table A]. Fitted costs add £390-£650 labour at an independent specialist, bringing the total to £1,500-£2,800 for a fitted rebuilt engine.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mitsubishi ASX 1.6?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning is a rattling noise on cold start that lasts 1-2 seconds, caused by a worn hydraulic tensioner. As wear progresses, you may notice rough idle, poor fuel economy, sluggish performance, or a check engine light with cam/crank correlation codes (P0016/P0017).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi ASX 1.6?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2014-2019 ASX 1.6 valued at £5,000-£14,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,200-£2,200 supply-only (£1,500-£2,800 fitted) is typically well within the vehicle's value. For very early 2010-2013 examples valued under £4,000, a used engine is often more cost-effective than a rebuilt unit.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mitsubishi ASX 1.6 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical 4A92 engine replacement takes 7-10 hours of labour at an independent specialist [estimated from standard 1.6-litre transverse four-cylinder fitting time]. Supply-only engines are usually delivered within 3-5 working days, with supply-and-fit turnaround typically 3-5 days from booking to collection.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Mitsubishi ASX 1.6 and the 2.0 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0-litre petrol (4B11) produces 147 hp, while the 1.6 (4A92) produces 117 hp. The 4A92 is more fuel-efficient (up to 48.7 mpg combined) and carries a lower insurance group, but the 4B11 offers significantly more performance. Both use timing chains, but the 4A92's timing chain is a more common replacement item at high mileage.

mainEntity.name: What is the Mitsubishi ASX 1.6 4A92 engine lifespan?

acceptedAnswer.text: With regular oil changes using 5W-30 and timely attention to timing chain wear, the 4A92 can achieve 150,000-200,000 miles. Oil consumption from piston ring wear typically becomes noticeable after 100,000 miles, and timing chain wear often requires attention between 80,000-150,000 miles.

This naturally aspirated unit remained largely unchanged across the model's full 2010-2024 production run, with only minor emissions updates.

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi ASX 1.6 (4A92) Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mitsubishi 4A92 1.6 petrol engine is a durable unit with a chain-driven valvetrain that can achieve around 250,000 km with proper maintenance . However, it has some well-documented weaknesses - timing chain wear, oil consumption, and oil starvation risks are the primary failure points that drive replacement decisions for ASX 1.6 owners. Rebuilt 4A92 engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - Why the Mitsubishi ASX 1.6 (4A92) Chain Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain, tensioner and guides rely on clean, correct-spec engine oil. Extended oil change intervals, oil sludge, or using incorrect viscosity can accelerate wear. Symptoms include rattling at cold start, rough idle, and check engine lights with cam/crank correlation faults (e.g., P0016/P0017) .

If the chain has already snapped or you've got rod knock from oil starvation, a rebuilt unit with upgraded components and full warranty is a better long-term investment than a patch-up repair on an already-compromised bottom end.

problems.group: Oil Consumption and Piston Ring Wear
problems.h4: Oil Consumption and Piston Ring Wear - 4A92's Age-Related Oil Burn
problems.rootCause: The 4A92 can develop oil consumption from piston ring wear, and in some cases, oil starvation can lead to connecting rod bearing wear . The engine also has no hydraulic lifters, requiring valve clearance adjustment which is often neglected, contributing to valve train wear .

repairOptions.longevity: For heavy oil consumption where rebuild is viable but replacement isn't necessary

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, fresh rings and bearings, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: For 4A92 with scoring or crankshaft damage from oil starvation

problems.recommendation: [2-3 honest sentences] If you're adding a litre of oil every 600 miles, a piston ring replacement is a viable mid-range repair at around £1,200-£1,800 from a specialist. If the engine has been run low on oil and has already developed rod knock, skip the repair and go straight to a rebuilt unit - a used engine of unknown history is a gamble on the same design weakness.
